articles.title: Yalta 2.0 in the making? Nuclear arms, two wars on the table as Trump, Xi and Putin meet
articles.summary: In a meeting that could reshape the global geopolitical order, US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir
articles.body: In a meeting that could reshape the global geopolitical order, US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to hold historic trilateral talks in China on Thursday, bringing together the leaders of three of the world's most powerful countries at a time of escalating international tensions.The meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen comes against the backdrop of two ongoing wars, the expiration of a key US-Russia nuclear arms control treaty, growing competition over artificial intelligence (AI) and unresolved trade disputes. The discussions could also test whether personal diplomacy between the three leaders can translate into concrete agreements on some of the world's most pressing security challenges.The gathering has drawn comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference, when the leaders of the United States, the Soviet Union and Britain came together towards the end of World War II to discuss the defeat of Nazi Germany and the political future of post-war Europe. However, unlike Yalta, where the three Allied powers were negotiating the future of a continent devastated by war, the Shenzhen meeting brings together leaders whose countries are competing for influence across multiple regions.The symbolism is particularly striking. Nearly eight decades after the Yalta Conference, the leaders of Washington, Moscow and Beijing are meeting at a time when the international system is increasingly shaped by great-power rivalry, competing security interests and questions over the future of the existing global order.Trump, who has repeatedly projected himself as a dealmaker capable of negotiating with rival leaders, has presented the meeting as an opportunity to discuss nuclear arms control and explore ways to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran. However, expectations of an immediate breakthrough remain limited, with major differences separating the three countries.From Yalta to Shenzhen: Are three powers preparing to shape the world order?The comparison with Yalta is rooted in the strategic importance of the three countries represented at the meeting and the possibility that decisions taken by their leaders could have consequences far beyond their borders.The Yalta Conference, held from February 4 to 11, 1945, brought together US President Franklin D Roosevelt, Soviet leader Joseph Stalin and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill in Crimea. The meeting took place as the defeat of Nazi Germany became increasingly inevitable.The three leaders discussed the final military campaign against Germany, the occupation of the country after its surrender, the establishment of the United Nations and the political restructuring of Europe. They also reached understandings on the division of Germany into occupation zones and the Soviet Union's role in the post-war European settlement.However, the agreements also exposed competing visions for Europe's future. Differences over the political direction of Eastern European countries, particularly Poland, contributed to tensions between the Western powers and the Soviet Union. These disagreements eventually became part of the broader confrontation that developed into the Cold War.The Shenzhen meeting is not a formal equivalent of Yalta. The geopolitical circumstances are different, and there is no indication that the three leaders intend to negotiate a comprehensive division of territories or spheres of influence.Nevertheless, the presence of the American, Russian and Chinese presidents at the same table carries considerable strategic weight. Together, their countries possess the world's largest nuclear arsenals, hold permanent seats on the United Nations Security Council and exercise considerable influence over international security, trade, technology and energy markets.The central question is whether the meeting will produce a framework for cooperation or reinforce the idea that global affairs are increasingly being shaped through negotiations among major powers, sometimes without the direct participation of countries most affected by their decisions.Nuclear arms control: Can Trump bring Washington, Moscow and Beijing together?Nuclear arms control is expected to be one of the most consequential issues discussed during the meeting.The last remaining nuclear arms control treaty between the United States and Russia, known as New START, expired in February 2026. The agreement placed limits on the two countries' deployed strategic nuclear warheads and delivery systems and provided mechanisms for transparency and verification.Its expiration has removed a key framework governing the world's two largest nuclear arsenals.Trump has expressed interest in negotiating a new agreement that would include China alongside Russia and the United States. He has described his proposal as a "new, improved and modernised" deal.However, bringing Beijing into a trilateral nuclear arms control framework presents a major challenge.China's nuclear arsenal is estimated to contain more than 600 warheads, considerably fewer than the more than 5,000 warheads believed to be held by each of the United States and Russia. Beijing has therefore been reluctant to accept restrictions designed around the much larger arsenals of the other two countries.From China's perspective, agreeing to numerical limits at its current level could constrain its ability to expand its nuclear deterrent while Washington and Moscow retain substantially larger stockpiles.For the United States and Russia, meanwhile, the absence of a binding framework raises concerns about transparency, strategic stability and the possibility of an unrestricted nuclear competition.Daryl Kimball, executive director of the Arms Control Association, said Trump's diplomatic initiative could potentially provide the starting point for more sustained negotiations, but warned against expecting immediate results."We need more than diplomatic theater and photo opportunities between Xi, Putin, and Trump at APEC," Kimball said. "And one meeting will not likely produce dramatic breakthroughs."The challenge is therefore not simply bringing the three leaders together. It is finding common ground between countries with different nuclear capabilities, strategic priorities and perceptions of security threats.Ukraine and Iran wars: Can three leaders negotiate an end to two conflicts?The wars in Ukraine and Iran are also expected to feature prominently in the discussions.Trump has indicated that he wants to use his relationship with Xi and Putin to explore ways of ending both conflicts. Kremlin foreign affairs adviser Yuri Ushakov said Putin, Trump and Xi would likely discuss the war in Ukraine, although the agenda had not been finalised.For Moscow, the meeting offers an opportunity to discuss the Ukraine conflict directly with Washington and Beijing. Russia has faced extensive Western sanctions since its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, while China has continued to maintain economic relations with Moscow.China's economic engagement has provided Russia with an important source of support as it seeks to withstand Western pressure.The presence of Xi could therefore be important to any diplomatic initiative involving Moscow, although Beijing's interests do not necessarily align with Washington's approach to ending the conflict.The diplomatic significance of the meeting is also shaped by the recent deterioration in relations between Washington and Kyiv. Trump has rejected additional sanctions against Russia, while disruptions in satellite support for Ukrainian military operations have raised questions about the continuity of American assistance.Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX operates satellite systems used by Ukraine, is also accompanying the US delegation, although he has so far maintained a low profile.The Iran conflict presents another complicated challenge. Trump has taken military action against Iran, while China and Russia have maintained economic and strategic engagement with Tehran.The three countries therefore approach the conflict from different positions, making a common diplomatic framework difficult to achieve.A further concern is the absence of the countries directly involved in these conflicts from the negotiating table. Ukraine is not part of the trilateral meeting, even though its territory and security are at the centre of discussions about the war with Russia.Similarly, the absence of other regional stakeholders could limit the scope of any understanding reached on Iran.This approach reflects Trump's preference for direct negotiations between powerful leaders. However, it also raises questions about whether agreements reached without the participation of countries directly affected by a conflict can translate into lasting settlements.Trump, Xi and Putin: Personal relationships versus strategic interestsTrump has repeatedly argued that his personal relationships with world leaders give him an advantage in international negotiations. His meetings with Xi and Putin are an important test of that approach.Xi made a high-profile gesture ahead of the trilateral meeting by personally greeting Trump as Air Force One arrived at the airport on Wednesday. The two leaders shook hands and exchanged a one-armed hug on the airport tarmac.The Chinese president also held separate discussions with Putin, whom he addressed as "my old friend". Putin responded by describing Xi as his "dear friend".Their exchanges reflected the closer strategic relationship between Beijing and Moscow, which has strengthened amid Western sanctions against Russia."China-Russia relations have remained steadfast through storms while taking a long-term view," Xi said to Putin. "They have brought greater stability and certainty to a world marked by intertwined changes and turbulence."The two leaders also discussed the Ukraine conflict and Trump's diplomatic representatives attempting to negotiate an end to the war, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state news agency RIA Novosti.The relationship between Xi and Putin is based on shared strategic interests, including opposition to what both governments describe as Western dominance of the international system. Their cooperation has expanded across trade, energy, military engagement and diplomatic coordination.Trump, meanwhile, has sought to cultivate relationships with both leaders despite the strategic competition between their countries and the United States.The distinction is important. Personal rapport may help facilitate communication, but it does not necessarily overcome differences in national interests.For Trump, the meeting provides an opportunity to demonstrate that Washington can engage directly with Beijing and Moscow. For Xi, hosting the leaders offers an opportunity to project China's diplomatic influence. For Putin, direct engagement with the US president provides an opportunity to demonstrate that Russia remains an important player in international affairs despite Western isolation efforts.US-China trade tensions and the AI race add another dimensionBeyond security and military issues, trade and technology competition are expected to shape the discussions between Trump and Xi.The United States and China remain locked in a broader economic contest involving tariffs, rare earth minerals, advanced semiconductors and artificial intelligence.The trade truce reached between the two countries last year, following a series of reciprocal tariff increases, is due to expire by January 10 next year.Before the APEC summit, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer held discussions with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng.Following the meeting, American officials said China had not fully honoured commitments made during last year's Trump-Xi meeting. These included increasing purchases of American agricultural products and easing restrictions on the export of rare earth minerals used in electronics manufacturing.Rare earth elements have become a major source of geopolitical leverage because they are essential for producing advanced electronics, electric vehicles, defence equipment and other high-technology products.The artificial intelligence race has added another layer to the rivalry.Washington has sought to restrict China's access to advanced American semiconductors that can be used to develop sophisticated AI models. Beijing, meanwhile, is attempting to strengthen its domestic semiconductor industry and reduce dependence on American technology.The dispute has also involved Nvidia, one of the world's leading AI chip manufacturers, and questions surrounding China's access to advanced computing hardware.Trump has so far held back from imposing tougher restrictions on China's access to advanced chips, suggesting that he does not want to aggravate relations with Beijing ahead of negotiations.The competing interests make the technology issue particularly sensitive. Both countries recognise the strategic importance of AI, but neither wants to give the other an advantage in a technology race that could influence economic growth, military capabilities and global influence.Trade has also become a foreign policy instrument in Trump's approach to Russia. His administration has considered the possibility of easing restrictions on trade with Moscow as an incentive for ending the Ukraine war.China and Russia, meanwhile, have continued economic engagement with Iran despite American military action against the country. The conflict has also affected global energy prices and economic growth.What the Shenzhen meeting means for the global orderThe meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin comes at a time when the post-Cold War international order is facing growing pressure from geopolitical conflicts, economic competition and the weakening of traditional diplomatic arrangements.The three leaders represent countries with considerable influence over the global security architecture. Their decisions on nuclear weapons, regional conflicts, trade and technology could have consequences extending well beyond their bilateral relationships.The Yalta comparison is therefore relevant not because the Shenzhen meeting is expected to produce a formal division of the world, but because it brings together three powerful leaders at a moment when the rules governing international relations are being contested.There is also a fundamental difference between the two gatherings. At Yalta, the Allied leaders were negotiating the arrangements for a world emerging from a devastating global war. In Shenzhen, the three leaders are attempting to manage conflicts and rivalries within an international system that remains deeply interconnected.Whether the meeting becomes a turning point or remains largely symbolic will depend on what follows the diplomatic exchanges.A breakthrough in nuclear arms control would require sustained negotiations and mechanisms for verification. Ending the wars in Ukraine and Iran would require agreements addressing the security concerns and political interests of the countries involved. Similarly, reducing trade and technology tensions would demand compromises that go beyond personal assurances.For now, the significance of the Shenzhen meeting lies in the fact that Washington, Moscow and Beijing are engaging directly at a time when their decisions carry consequences for the rest of the world.The question is whether this gathering will mark the beginning of a new framework for managing global power rivalries or become another high-profile diplomatic encounter without lasting agreements.You use AI every day. articles.title: Flying too low? NTSB reveals how helicopter crashed into Florida bay, killing pilot
articles.summary: A helicopter crashed in Biscayne Bay earlier this month after it hit the water during a turn.
articles.body: A helicopter crashed in Biscayne Bay earlier this month after it hit the water during a turn. The aircraft was flying extremely close to the surface, the National Transportation Safety Board said on Wednesday. One person died, and two others were critically injured.The Robinson R44 II helicopter crashed on November 4 near Bill Baggs State Park, off Key Biscayne. It was filming a powerboating event taking place offshore, the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office said.According to news agency AP, the pilot died in the crash. A photographer and a videographer on board suffered injuries.The NTSB's preliminary report said the helicopter was making very low turns, extremely close to the water. Some of its doors had been removed to make photography and videography easier.During one turn, the rotor blades struck the water. This caused the helicopter to crash.The photographer told investigators that the helicopter was flying low beside the right side of a boat. It then turned and moved ahead of the boat to get a “good shot” as the boat passed underneath. The videographer then saw the rotor blades hit the water, the report said.News footage showed the helicopter upside down underwater. Two yellow emergency floats were attached to its landing skids. These floats are designed to help keep a helicopter afloat during a water landing.People in nearby boats called for help. One person also tried to rescue a victim, Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz said.Rescue teams from several local agencies reached the scene. The US Coast Guard and US Customs and Border Protection also joined the rescue operation.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: US judge extends order blocking Trump’s giant memorial arch in Washington
articles.summary: A US federal judge on Wednesday extended an order that prevents the Trump administration from starting construction of a giant memorial arch in
articles.body: A US federal judge on Wednesday extended an order that prevents the Trump administration from starting construction of a giant memorial arch in Washington, DC.The temporary order was due to expire on Thursday. However, US district Judge Tanya Chutkan extended it by another 14 days. This means construction will remain on hold until December 3 or until she decides on a request for a longer ban, according to news agency AP.Chutkan had first stopped the project on November 5. Her order came after the National capital planning commission approved the arch in an 8-4 vote. The decision came despite opposition from dozens of people who spoke at the hearing.The Trump administration had said construction could begin once the commission approved the project, the interior department gave its final clearance and the National park service published the required notice.The judge extended the order after lawyers representing the opponents of the project requested more time. Several groups have now filed separate lawsuits challenging the construction.Nicolas Sansone, a lawyer with the public citizen litigation group, welcomed the decision. The group is representing the plaintiffs in the original lawsuit.He said the situation had not changed since the judge first stepped in two weeks ago. He added that the additional pause would give the court time to consider their arguments for a longer ban on construction while the case continues.The White House criticised the ruling. Spokesman Davis Ingle called it another example of a district court blocking the construction of the planned Military Triumphal Arch.He said the monument was designed to unite the country. The administration would continue defending the project and was confident it would win the legal battle, he added.The district of Columbia and Virginia filed a lawsuit against the project on October 31. Chutkan combined their case with an earlier lawsuit filed by three Vietnam veterans and a retired architectural historian.Members of the Kennedy family filed a separate lawsuit on November 10. They raised concerns about the impact of the proposed 250-foot (76-metre) structure on relatives buried at Arlington National Cemetery.The Arlington county board also filed a lawsuit on October 8 in a federal court in Virginia. It challenged the speed of the project and the possible impact on the county, which is close to the proposed site.Chutkan said the 14-day extension was necessary because there had been no major changes in the case since her earlier order. She decided to keep the construction on hold until she rules on the request for a longer injunction.The arch is one of several projects Trump has pursued as part of his plans to reshape Washington. These include renovating a historic public golf course and threatening to demolish the John F. Kennedy Center for the performing arts.Several of these projects have faced legal challenges. They could also come under greater scrutiny when democrats take control of Congress.The federal government filed an appeal on Thursday against a separate 14-day order that had stopped work on the golf course project.The original lawsuit against the arch was filed by three veterans and a retired architectural historian. They asked the court to stop the administration and the National Park Service from taking any steps towards construction at memorial circle without approval from Congress.Opponents argue that the administration must get congressional approval before building the arch. They also say the 250-foot structure would affect views connecting important historic landmarks in Washington.The administration, however, argues that Congress had already approved the construction of a monument at memorial circle decades ago.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Maine town found $55,737 inside a safe abandoned in the woods; after four years without an owner coming forward, the money will help families pay winter heating bills
articles.summary: A Maine town is turning a mystery stash of more than $55,000 found inside a safe in the woods into heating assistance for local families.
articles.body: A Maine town is turning a mystery stash of more than $55,000 found inside a safe in the woods into heating assistance for local families. The cash was discovered in Falmouth in 2022 after a resident spotted the safe on a wooded trail near the town’s Central Fire Station. Police opened it and found $55,737 inside, but no owner came forward despite an investigation that included tracing the money to a New Hampshire bank and contacting other law enforcement agencies. The unexplained cash remained in police custody for four years before Falmouth officials decided to put it towards heating assistance as winter approaches.$55,737 found in Falmouth woods remained unclaimed for four yearsThe safe was found in August 2022 by a resident walking a trail between Falmouth’s Central Fire Station and nearby baseball fields. According to reporting from Independent via Yahoo News, police opened the safe and discovered $55,737 in cash. Investigators then tried to determine where the money came from, including checking with law enforcement agencies in Maine and New Hampshire.The cash was traced to a New Hampshire bank, which confirmed it had not been reported stolen. Police also publicised that they had found a large amount of unclaimed money, but no one came forward to claim it. Falmouth Police Chief John Kilbride said authorities kept the money for years in case it had been taken from someone who had not yet realised it was missing.The circumstances surrounding how the cash ended up in the woods remain unknown. Police ultimately processed it as unclaimed property after their efforts to identify an owner produced no answer.Falmouth will use mystery cash to help families with heating billsUnder Maine law, unclaimed money of this kind must be directed towards a charitable purpose. Falmouth Town Council voted to send the funds to the town’s Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, or LIHEAP, according to WGME.The decision comes as Maine households prepare for winter heating costs. Town officials said the unexpected funds could provide timely help to residents struggling with heating expenses. The money is expected to become available from January.Falmouth Town Council Chair Bryce Hawke described the money as an unusual source of community funding because it did not come from taxpayers or an established town programme. The town’s decision means the unexplained cash discovered in the woods will now be used to support residents facing one of the most immediate costs of the winter season.The identity of whoever placed the money in the woods remains a mystery, but after four years without a claimant, the cash is set to serve a very different purpose from whatever brought it there in the first place.You use AI every day. articles.title: US Federal Court judge 'cancels' fixed terms of admission for F, J, and I non-immigrant visas; says that it is against Congress’s intent in creating the subject visa programs: Here's why it is good news for international students
articles.summary: International students in the US have received a major relief (at least for the time being) after a federal court struck down a regulation that sought to
articles.body: International students in the US have received a major relief (at least for the time being) after a federal court struck down a regulation that sought to introduce fixed stay limits for foreign students, exchange visitors and foreign media representatives. A federal district court in Massachusetts ruled against the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) regulation, finding that it went against Congress's intent when it created the F, J and I visa programmes. The court also found that the regulation violated the Administrative Procedure Act (APA).The decision was delivered by Judge Dennis Saylor in the case Presidents’ Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration et al. v. US Department of Homeland Security et al., filed in August 2026.What was the US visa rule that the court struck downThe DHS regulation aimed to replace the existing duration-of-status system with fixed periods of admission for certain non-immigrant visa holders. Under the duration-of-status system, foreign students and exchange visitors can generally remain in the US as long as they continue to meet the requirements of their authorised status. The proposed regulation sought to replace this arrangement with specific time limits on their stay.The rule covered three categories of non-immigrant visas:F-1 visas: For international students pursuing academic studies in the US.J-1 visas: For exchange visitors participating in approved exchange programmes.I visas: For representatives of foreign information media working in the US.The proposed changes also covered dependents of these visa holders.Why did the US court cancel the fixed admission ruleThe court found that the DHS regulation exceeded the department's authority and was inconsistent with Congress's intent in creating the F, J and I visa programmes. The ruling also stated that the regulation violated the Administrative Procedure Act, which sets requirements for how federal agencies introduce and implement rules.The legal challenge was filed in August 2026 by a coalition of educational organisations and unions. The groups included NAFSA, the Presidents’ Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration, the American Federation of Teachers and the United Auto Workers (UAW).They argued that replacing duration-of-status admissions with fixed periods would violate the Administrative Procedure Act. In September, the court had temporarily postponed the regulation's effective date while the legal proceedings continued. It has now vacated the rule.Why is the ruling good news for international studentsThe decision is significant for international students because the proposed regulation would have replaced the duration-of-status system with fixed admission periods. With the regulation vacated, the proposed fixed-term restrictions will not take effect under this rule. The existing duration-of-status framework remains in place, subject to the applicable immigration requirements.This is also relevant for exchange visitors and foreign media representatives covered by the J and I visa categories.However, the ruling may not be the final word on the matter as the Trump administration is expected to appeal the decision.Your child uses AI every day. articles.title: ‘I am not guilty’: Google refuses UK government plea to remove Russell Brand's video from YouTube
articles.summary: Google has declined a request from the UK government to remove a YouTube video in which jailed comedian Russell Brand maintains his innocence following
articles.body: Google has declined a request from the UK government to remove a YouTube video in which jailed comedian Russell Brand maintains his innocence following his conviction for rape and sexual assault.The BBC reported the development, citing Whitehall sources, after the Prison Service of England and Wales sought the video's removal following its publication by Brand’s wife, Laura Gallacher, on their joint YouTube channel.A Ministry of Justice (MoJ) spokesperson said it was “only right” to ask for content that was “distressing for victims” to be removed. The spokesperson added that while “removal ultimately depends on the platform's own terms”, the department strongly believes “YouTube should remove this content”.The video was shared on Sunday during an episode of the couple's Sunday Service with the Brands programme. Gallacher read out a handwritten message from Brand, in which he said, “Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for.”He added, “So something strange is happening.”The Prison Service formally asked YouTube to take down the video, citing concerns that it was offensive to Brand's victims and had reached a substantial audience. The BBC reported that officials had initially been told a minister met Google representatives to seek the deactivation of Brand's account.The request followed a separate move by Meta, which disabled Brand's Instagram and Facebook profiles. According to Sky News, a justice minister also met Google representatives to discuss removing his YouTube account.The Ministry of Justice has launched an investigation into whether Brand breached prison rules by arranging for a message from jail to be made public. Prisoners are allowed to maintain their innocence, but restrictions apply to public statements that could cause distress to victims and to communication with the media.A government spokesperson said, “We expect action to be taken if he's found to have broken the rules.” The spokesperson also said prisoners could not circumvent restrictions by having another person read out their comments.The message came a day after The Times published a report on Sunday identifying Mia Latter, 37, who had previously accused Brand of raping her when she was a teenager. Her allegations were not part of the criminal trial. Latter thanked the women who had spoken out against Brand, saying, “They put him away. Some women didn’t get the guilty verdict, but it was definitely a team effort, and I will forever be grateful to them.”Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison on November 9 after being convicted at Southwark Crown Court of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women between 2004 and 2009. Judge Joel Bennathan described him as a “sexual predator” and criticised his “staggering arrogance”, according to Deadline.Brand had maintained his innocence during the trial, telling the jury, “Consent is fundamental, essential, necessary, and in many ways more important than the sex itself.”You use AI every day. articles.title: 'World is peaceful when major countries are in harmony': Trump, Xi, Putin hold historic trilateral meeting at Shenzhen - top developments
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the 33rd
articles.body: US President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China's Shenzhen.The meeting brings together the leaders of three major powers at a time of growing geopolitical rivalry and uncertainty over the international order.Here are the top developmentsWhat the leaders said during the trilateral meetingDuring the meeting, Trump said that the three leaders are "uniquely positioned" to discuss ways to reduce nuclear weapons.He said that peace could never be achieved by declining opportunities for dialogue.“Too often, past leaders avoided talking to leaders they have disagreements with,” Trump said."Both the United States and China have an interest in ensuring that energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, and that Iran cannot, uh, have a nuclear weapon. We both feel that very strongly, on both points," Trump said during the meeting.Addressing the meeting, Xi said that healthy interactions between major countries were not optional but a necessity. He added that the world would descend into chaos if major powers fought.“The world is peaceful when major countries are in harmony,” Xi said, according to Chinese state media.Meanwhile, Putin told his Chinese and US counterparts that the three countries s can strengthen global stability if they cooperate constructively.Putin said he, Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump should discuss global and regional issues as well as energy security.Trump pitches US role in Asia-PacificEarlier during the APEC summit, Trump sought to underline Washington's longstanding presence and strategic interests in the Asia-Pacific region, amid China's growing economic and geopolitical influence."The United States has been a Pacific power for hundreds of years, and we continue to work to promote growth and stability, sovereignty, prosperity, and peace throughout this region," he said.Trump also referred to the domestic economic situation, claiming that inflation had fallen more than expected over the previous three months."The last three months, inflation was down to a number that was not expected," he said.His remarks come as Washington and Beijing continue to navigate trade disputes, competition over advanced technologies and differences over regional security.Trump opposes global curbs on superintelligence, calls it biggest technological shift since Industrial RevolutionTrump has opposed global regulations aimed at controlling or restricting the development of superintelligence (SI), saying Washington would not allow measures that could stifle the emerging technology and its potential to drive economic growth.Addressing the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, Trump described superintelligence as the greatest technological transformation since the Industrial Revolution and claimed that the United States was leading the world in its development."The United States is also proud to be the world leader in superintelligence, SI, the greatest technological transformation since the Industrial Revolution. It's amazing when you say that, but it seems to be true. Americans invented—we just invented SI, and it is unleashing extraordinary prosperity and growth for people all around the globe," Trump said.Xi calls for open trade and regional cooperationChinese President Xi Jinping, addressing the APEC summit, called for free and open trade, stronger regional cooperation and improved economic connectivity across the Asia-Pacific.Xi urged member economies to uphold open regionalism, remove barriers to trade and create more opportunities for economic growth. He also called for improved regional data governance and the promotion of smart customs systems to facilitate cross-border commerce."We must uphold open regionalism, steadily promote economy, build open but not exclusive cooperation," Xi said.He also called for efforts to "unblock economic channels" and advocated free and open trade amid continuing global trade tensions.Xi's remarks come as China seeks to strengthen its position in regional economic frameworks while facing growing trade and technology competition with the United States.Putin pitches Russian energy and logistics infrastructureRussian President Vladimir Putin, meanwhile, invited regional partners to use Russia's logistics infrastructure and sought to underline Moscow's contribution to Asia-Pacific energy security.Putin said Russia was contributing to regional energy security and that its partners could always count on Moscow. He also invited regional economies to make use of Russian logistics networks, adding that some partners were already doing so.Putin also expressed support for the APEC final communiqué.His remarks come as Russia seeks to strengthen economic and energy partnerships in Asia amid Western sanctions imposed following its invasion of Ukraine.Trump-Xi-Putin meeting: Nuclear arms and two wars on agendaThe high-profile trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin is expected to be one of the key developments of the APEC summit.The discussions are expected to focus on nuclear arms control, the ongoing wars in Ukraine and Iran, trade relations and competition over artificial intelligence.Trump has expressed interest in negotiating a new nuclear arms control agreement involving Washington, Moscow and Beijing following the expiration of the New START treaty between the United States and Russia in February 2026.However, differences in the nuclear capabilities of the three countries could complicate negotiations. China has an estimated arsenal of more than 600 nuclear warheads, compared with more than 5,000 each in the US and Russian stockpiles.The Ukraine conflict is another major issue, with Putin expected to discuss the war with Trump and Xi. The meeting also comes amid continuing tensions over Iran, where the interests of Washington, Beijing and Moscow remain sharply divided.Trade and technology are likely to feature prominently as well. The United States and China continue to face disagreements over tariffs, rare earth exports and access to advanced semiconductor technology used in AI development.The three leaders' engagement could provide an opportunity to discuss these challenges directly, although expectations of immediate agreements remain limited.The APEC summit has thus emerged as a major diplomatic platform for Washington, Beijing and Moscow to present their positions on regional economic cooperation, global security and the future of international trade.You use AI every day. articles.title: Hong Kong ends case against captain accused of damaging Baltic gas pipeline
articles.summary: Hong Kong has dropped its prosecution of the Chinese captain of a container ship accused of damaging a gas pipeline in the Baltic Sea in October 2023,
articles.body: Hong Kong has dropped its prosecution of the Chinese captain of a container ship accused of damaging a gas pipeline in the Baltic Sea in October 2023, according to media reports on Wednesday.Prosecutors told a magistrate's court that they could not contact several witnesses from mainland China. This led to the decision to drop the case, the reports said.Captain Wan Wenguo, who is in his 40s, is expected to be deported to mainland China. He has been in custody since December 2024, the South China Morning Post reported.Wan was the captain of the Hong Kong-registered container ship Newnew Polar Bear. He had pleaded not guilty to damaging a section of the 77-km Balticconnector gas pipeline between Estonia and Finland, cited by news agency Reuters.However, he admitted guilt to two lesser charges related to failing to meet safety requirements.Wan's lawyer, Jerry Chung, had earlier said that the prosecution planned to call 18 witnesses to testify.Finnish investigators believe the ship dragged its anchor across the seabed and damaged the pipeline. Tests also showed that a broken anchor found near the damaged pipeline belonged to the vessel. The ship was found to be missing an anchor.China had earlier promised Finland and Estonia that it would help with the investigation. Beijing also called for an objective and fair inquiry into the incident.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A great horned owl survived being struck by a tractor-trailer travelling at 65 mph, then remained trapped in its front air dam for about 70 miles before Pennsylvania rescuers freed it with few injuries
articles.summary: In horrific news from Pennsylvania, a great horned owl thankfully survived being struck by a tractor-trailer travelling at 65 mph.
articles.body: In horrific news from Pennsylvania, a great horned owl thankfully survived being struck by a tractor-trailer travelling at 65 mph. What’s more, it remained trapped in its front air dam for about 70 miles before Pennsylvania rescuers freed it with few injuries. We bet that owl has a story to tell when he gets home.While most birds would struggle to survive an impact of that magnitude, this particular owl appears to have had luck on its side. What followed was an unexpected journey across Pennsylvania, with the bird stuck in a rather unusual hiding spot: the front of a moving truck.An unexpected passengerThe incident took place in Pennsylvania, when a driver for Old Dominion Freight Line struck the owl while travelling at approximately 65 mph. The driver knew she had hit the bird and even noted the mile marker where the collision occurred. What she did not realise was that the owl had become lodged in the truck's front air dam.An air dam is the structure fitted beneath the front bumper of a vehicle. It helps manage airflow around the vehicle, particularly at higher speeds. In this case, the truck's fibreglass air dam became an unlikely hiding place for an injured bird.The driver continued towards the company's terminal in Carlisle, unaware that she had an unexpected passenger. By the time the truck arrived, the owl had travelled approximately 70 miles, still stuck headfirst in the structure. The wildlife centre later described the journey as one of the most astonishing survival stories it had encountered.A rescue effort after hoursOnce the owl was discovered, employees at the trucking terminal contacted Raven Ridge Wildlife Center in Washington Boro, Pennsylvania. The centre received an after-hours call from the company, explaining that the bird was still alive but trapped.The maintenance team at Old Dominion Freight Line worked to carefully free the owl from the air dam. Once released, however, the bird attempted to fly but could not manage it and needed medical attention.With the wildlife centre more than an hour away, volunteers stepped in to coordinate its transport. One volunteer collected the owl from the terminal, while another met them along the way to help bring it safely to the rehabilitation centre. It was a collective effort involving the trucking company's employees and wildlife rescuers, all working to give the bird a fighting chance.A surprisingly clean bill of healthWhen the owl finally arrived at Raven Ridge, its condition was better than anyone could have expected. Its feathers were dishevelled, understandably, but the initial examination revealed no broken wings, broken legs or open wounds.The most significant injury was to its left eye, which had suffered bleeding and swelling following the collision. The centre arranged a full examination with a veterinarian, who was reportedly amazed by how little trauma the bird had sustained.Considering that the owl had not only been struck by a moving vehicle but had also remained lodged in its front structure for 70 miles at highway speed, its condition was remarkable. The centre shared photographs and details of the rescue on Facebook, expressing disbelief at the bird's survival. It described the owl as perhaps the luckiest it had ever encountered.The road back to the wildFor now, the great horned owl is under observation at Raven Ridge Wildlife Center while its eye heals. Although surviving the collision is an encouraging start, the bird still needs to demonstrate that it can fly properly before it can be returned to the wild.The centre has planned the owl’s eventual release. Once it has recovered and staff have been able to observe it flying outdoors, they intend to drive it back the same 70 miles to the area where it was originally struck.They made this decision keeping in mind that releasing a wild animal in unfamiliar surroundings can make it harder for it to find food, shelter and suitable territory. Returning it close to where it was found gives it a better chance of resuming its life in familiar surroundings.This particular owl has already survived an ordeal that would have been difficult to imagine, and its recovery is a reminder of what timely intervention can do for injured wildlife. And hopefully, its next 70-mile journey will be a considerably more peaceful one.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A London woman took her neighbours to court after they allegedly forced her garden gate twice and changed its lock; a judge ordered a father and son to pay £20,000 in legal costs
articles.summary: A London woman who withdrew permission for neighbours to use a passageway leading to a shared garden over privacy concerns has secured an interim court
articles.body: A London woman who withdrew permission for neighbours to use a passageway leading to a shared garden over privacy concerns has secured an interim court order after a dispute involving allegations of trespass and harassment. Musician Jodie Schloss took legal action against a father and son after the gate to the passageway was allegedly forced open twice and its lock changed without her knowledge. The row at a residential property in Swiss Cottage also involved the family leaving their laundry to dry on her private patio. Judge Stephen Hellman ordered the two men to pay approximately £20,000 in legal costs and accepted legally binding undertakings preventing them from entering her passageway or patio without permission.Jodie Schloss objected to neighbours walking past her front doorAccording to The Independent, the claimant was musician Jodie Schloss, who lives in a garden flat at a Victorian villa in Strathray Gardens, Swiss Cottage. The passageway runs alongside her property and provides access to the garden at the rear of the building. For around 30 years, residents of other flats had also used the route to reach the garden, with Schloss having previously provided them with keys.However, the arrangement changed in August 2025 when Schloss withdrew her consent for other residents to use the passageway, citing privacy concerns. Her barrister, John Clargo, told the court that she no longer wanted people walking so close to her front door, describing it as an "invasion of her sense of privacy". Although other residents had previously used the route, Clargo argued that they did not have a right to use either the passageway or the garden. Robin Larkins, one of the neighbours involved in the dispute, had his own direct access to the garden through the back door of his flat.Dispute escalated after neighbours allegedly damaged gate and changed its lockThe disagreement intensified after Schloss withdrew permission. Clargo told the court that on 1 September 2025, Derek Larkins insisted he had a right to use the passageway, while his son Robin threatened to rip out the gate. Schloss subsequently discovered damage to the lock and, after returning to collect her belongings on 6 September, found further damage. Her barrister said CCTV footage led her to believe Robin had been responsible for the later damage.Clargo also told the court that Robin changed the lock on the gate on 2 October 2025 without providing Schloss with a key, despite a request from her solicitor. She subsequently changed the locks back. On 22 March 2026, Derek allegedly forced the lock, and the two men used the passageway on that date and again on 24 March. The dispute also involved an incident on 9 April 2026, when laundry belonging to Robin Larkins' family was hung out to dry on Schloss's private patio. Robin said his cleaner had put the washing there without realising and had been told not to repeat it.London woman sought injunction to stop neighbours entering her propertySchloss brought proceedings alleging trespass and harassment and sought an injunction to prevent further incursions onto her property. During the hearing, Robin Larkins represented himself and argued that the dispute was about protecting the other leaseholders' access to the communal garden. He told the judge that he had direct access to the garden from his own flat, but believed the other residents should also be able to use it because they had enjoyed access for 30 years and contributed towards its maintenance through their service charges.After a three-hour hearing, Judge Stephen Hellman, sitting at Mayor's and City County Court, accepted legally binding undertakings from Derek and Robin Larkins not to enter Schloss's passageway or patio again without permission, pending a full trial. The judge said he could understand how Schloss's letter withdrawing access must have come as a shock to the other residents. However, he also noted that the conduct involving the forced gate justified a substantial costs order.Court ordered father and son to pay around £20,000 in legal costsAccording to Gatehouse Chambers, the court ordered the defendants to pay approximately £20,000 in legal costs and found that the forced entry to the passageway justified an order on the indemnity basis, despite the hearing concerning an application for interim relief. The chambers said the judge granted relief in the claimant's favour after hearing evidence of two occasions when the gate was forced, and the lock was changed without her knowledge.The undertakings mean that Derek and Robin Larkins are legally bound not to enter Schloss's passageway or patio without her permission. However, the dispute has not yet reached a full trial. The case is due to return to court at a later date unless the parties settle first. Judge Hellman also warned the defendants that they could face substantially higher legal costs if they continued to contest the case and ultimately lost.You use AI every day. articles.title: 2 dead, 6 injured after Fortuner rams into autorickshaw near Delhi's Kashmere gate
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Two people were killed and six others injured after a speeding SUV rammed into an autorickshaw in north Delhi during the intervening night of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Two people were killed and six others injured after a speeding SUV rammed into an autorickshaw in north Delhi during the intervening night of November 17 and 18, police said.The accident took place on Yudhisthir Setu, within the jurisdiction of Kashmere Gate police station, when a Toyota Fortuner allegedly crashed into the three-wheeler.According to police, eight people sustained injuries in the collision. An FIR was initially registered under Sections 281 and 125(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deal with rash driving and acts endangering life or personal safety.However, two of the injured later died, following which Section 105 of the BNS was added to the case.Police said efforts were underway to identify and apprehend the accused. Further details about the circumstances leading to the collision are awaited.In a separate incident earlier this month, two men were killed after a truck collided with a scooty near the old police station in Delhi's Khajuri Khas area late on Monday night, officials said on November 3.Police received a call about the accident at around 11.55pm. A team rushed to the spot and found two men critically injured.The victims were identified as Santosh, 30, a resident of Pakki Khajuri, and Pawan, 33, who lived in Gali Number 24 in Khajuri Khas.One of the injured men was taken to JPC Hospital by his family, while police personnel shifted the other to the same facility. Both were declared brought dead by doctors.Their bodies were later taken to Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital for post-mortem examinations.Police recovered the concrete mixer truck involved in the collision from the spot. articles.title: In 2016, Elton John gave a piano to a London railway station for anyone to play; 10 years later, the instrument is going to auction with an estimate of £120,000 to £250,000 to benefit his AIDS foundation
articles.summary: Elton John’s signed Yamaha piano, which has stood at London’s St Pancras International station for a decade, is going to auction with an estimate of
articles.body: Elton John’s signed Yamaha piano, which has stood at London’s St Pancras International station for a decade, is going to auction with an estimate of £120,000 to £250,000. The proceeds will support the Elton John AIDS Foundation, according to The Auction Collective and AOL. The piano was gifted to the station in February 2016 after John surprised passengers with an impromptu performance. Since then, it has been played by thousands of members of the public as well as musicians including Alicia Keys, John Legend, Jeff Goldblum, Tom Odell, and Jools Holland. Read more about it, as per the reports, here:How the piano became famousElton John first sat down at the piano on February 4, 2016, to celebrate the release of his 33rd studio album, Wonderful Crazy Night. He performed a medley of songs including “Tiny Dancer,” “Your Song,” “Bennie and the Jets,” and “Candle in the Wind.”Afterwards, he signed the instrument and left it at the station for the public to enjoy. His message on the piano read, “Enjoy this piano. It’s a gift. Love, Elton John.”The piano became a fixture at St Pancras, giving travellers and visitors a chance to stop, play, and share a moment of music. Peter Martin-Jones, head of marketing at St Pancras International, said the instrument had played a special role in the station’s story over the past decade.Why it is being soldThe auction is being held ahead of World AIDS Day on December 1. The proceeds will go to the Elton John AIDS Foundation, which John established in 1992.The foundation has raised more than $660 million and supported more than 3,236 programmes across 108 countries. It works to tackle discrimination, prevent HIV infections, and improve access to treatment and care.The total hammer price, minus applicable taxes and the auction platform’s nine percent fee, will be donated to the foundation. This means the final sale price will directly support the organisation’s work.What the auction offersThe St Pancras Piano is being offered by The Auction Collective, with bidding opening on Friday, November 20, and closing on December 2. The estimate is £120,000 to £250,000, reflecting the piano’s history, signature, and cultural significance.The piano will return to St Pancras International for a one day public display on Saturday, November 21. This gives visitors one final opportunity to see the instrument at the station before it moves to a new home.Those interested in bidding can register through the Elton John AIDS Foundation website. The auction is expected to attract collectors, music fans, and institutions interested in owning a piece of British pop culture.Why the piano mattersThe piano is more than a musical instrument. It is a piece of Elton John’s history, a public gift, and a symbol of how music can bring people together in unexpected places.Over the past decade, it has been played by both famous artists and ordinary passengers. That mix of celebrity and everyday use gives the piano a story that few auction lots can match.Anne Aslett, chief executive of the Elton John AIDS Foundation, described the piano as a unique piece of Elton’s musical history. She said its auction to mark World AIDS Day will raise vital funds for HIV prevention, treatment, and compassionate care.What happens nextWith bidding opening on November 20, the piano’s next chapter is about to begin. The final sale will determine whether it reaches the lower end of the estimate or goes beyond it.For St Pancras, the sale marks the end of a decade long chapter. For the Elton John AIDS Foundation, it represents a new opportunity to turn a beloved public instrument into support for its mission.The piano’s journey shows how a single act of generosity can create lasting impact. What began as a surprise performance in a London station has become a fundraising effort with global reach.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Bangladesh violence: Muhammad Yunus’ ancestral home set ablaze in Chattogram amid unrest
articles.summary: Unidentified attackers on Thursday set ablaze the ancestral home of former interim government chief Muhammad Yunus in Chattogram, as violence intensified
articles.body: Unidentified attackers on Thursday set ablaze the ancestral home of former interim government chief Muhammad Yunus in Chattogram, as violence intensified across Bangladesh, with crude bomb explosions reported in the capital. The incidents came amid a nationwide shutdown called by the banned Awami League.At least four people were injured in the violence, which involved explosions, arson and vandalism despite heightened security measures. The attacks took place ahead of the "lockdown" called by the Awami League, led by former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, to coincide with the anniversary of a special tribunal verdict that sentenced her to death in absentia last year.Unidentified arsonists targeted Yunus's paternal residence in the Panchlaish area of Chattogram. The attack followed reports of fires at several branches of his Grameen Bank in different parts of the country, including Sylhet, Rajshahi, Barishal and Faridpur.Police and witnesses reported multiple crude bomb explosions in Dhaka during the early hours of Thursday. Security personnel were deployed at major flyovers, while vehicles were checked at entry and exit points across the capital.The unrest also saw attacks on properties linked to rival political groups. Newspaper reports said suspected activists of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) attacked or set fire to the residences of two Awami League leaders in Dhaka.Security tightened, hundreds arrested ahead of shutdownAuthorities stepped up security across the country, deploying thousands of paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel in sensitive areas, including southwestern Gopalganj district, Hasina's birthplace.According to BDnews24, police arrested 565 people in a 24-hour operation in Dhaka alone ahead of the shutdown. Among those detained was former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid, who served in Hasina's cabinet. He was reportedly picked up from his residence around midnight on Wednesday.Police personnel were also deployed at major intersections and transport routes to prevent further violence and monitor suspicious movements.The unrest has spread beyond the capital, with attacks and clashes reported across several districts. Police said two local ruling party leaders were killed in western Narail district after Awami League activists allegedly attacked a BNP street march.Two other people, including a local BNP leader and a transport worker, were killed in separate incidents in southwestern Faridpur and Pirojpur on Tuesday and Wednesday nights.Media reports also said at least two BNP offices and the residence of a party leader were set on fire. In response, at least two Awami League offices and five properties belonging to leaders of the banned party were reportedly torched over the past two days.Dozens of crude bombs were also reported to have exploded, while vehicles were set ablaze in 28 of Bangladesh's 64 administrative districts.Tarique Rahman calls for unity against Awami LeagueAmid the escalating violence, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman appealed to democratic forces to unite against what he described as an attempt by the Awami League to return to power.Describing the banned party as a "terrorist outfit" and a "fallen, defeated, and ousted fascist force", Rahman called for coordinated efforts to prevent its resurgence."Let us once again unite in the spirit of 2024, when we drove the autocratic forces out of this country, and ensure that those forces are decisively defeated," Rahman said in a parliamentary address on Tuesday night.Ahead of his address during the concluding sitting of the current parliamentary session, Rahman met BNP lawmakers and asked them to return to their constituencies to maintain a visible presence on the ground.According to The Daily Star, he also urged party lawmakers not to depend exclusively on government machinery and the administration to counter Awami League activists. Instead, he asked them to coordinate with grassroots leaders and party workers.The BNP's former ally Jamaat-e-Islami is currently the main opposition party in parliament.Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has promised to identify those responsible for the violence and initiate strict legal action against them, using available audio and video evidence.Why has violence intensified in Bangladesh?The latest unrest is linked to growing political tensions following the ouster of Hasina's government in August 2024 and subsequent legal action against the former prime minister and her party.Hasina, 79, has been living in India since August 5, 2024, when she fled Bangladesh following a student-led uprising known as the July Uprising. The movement brought an end to her Awami League government's tenure after weeks of protests and violence.Bangladesh has since sought her extradition from India.The Awami League called Thursday's shutdown to coincide with the anniversary of a special tribunal verdict that sentenced Hasina to death in absentia last year on charges of crimes against humanity linked to the crackdown on the uprising.The interim administration led by Yunus, which assumed power following Hasina's departure, subsequently disbanded the Awami League and initiated legal proceedings against thousands of its leaders and activists. Many were arrested on charges including murder and involvement in violence during the uprising.During Yunus's tenure, properties and landmarks associated with Hasina's family and the Awami League were also targeted.Hasina's father and Bangladesh's founding leader, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, had his Dhanmondi residence set on fire and demolished in phases by mobs believed to be supporters of the uprising. Several landmarks associated with the 1971 Liberation War were also vandalised.At the time, Shafiqul Alam, the chief spokesperson of the Yunus-led interim administration, described the mob as a "pressure group".Hasina's planned return adds to political tensionsPolitical tensions have intensified since July, when Hasina first announced plans to return to Bangladesh voluntarily from India in December, despite the death sentence against her.She said she was willing to return to face legal proceedings, while the Bangladeshi government continued to seek her extradition under a bilateral treaty with India.Her renewed declaration earlier this month that she would return in December at "any cost" reportedly triggered fresh tensions within the country.The latest violence initially erupted in Hasina's southwestern hometown of Tungipara after dozens of youths suspected of being Awami League supporters were arrested on Tuesday.A local journalist reported that police personnel had vacated a police station after hundreds of people surrounded it. Nearly 30 suspected Awami League activists had been detained there earlier.The attack on Yunus's ancestral home and the reported arson at Grameen Bank branches mark a new development in the unrest, which had largely involved clashes between rival political groups and attacks on properties associated with the Awami League.With violence spreading across multiple districts, the government faces mounting pressure to restore order as political tensions continue to deepen ahead of Hasina's proposed return.

articles.title: Bruce Springsteen’s archive began as a fan collection in 2001; 25 years later, a $50 million, 32,000-square-foot New Jersey music centre is open to the public and preserves more than 48,000 items
articles.summary: What began as an effort by Bruce Springsteen fans to preserve newspaper clippings, photographs and memorabilia has grown into one of the most significant
articles.body: What began as an effort by Bruce Springsteen fans to preserve newspaper clippings, photographs and memorabilia has grown into one of the most significant public collections dedicated to American music. The Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music, located at Monmouth University in New Jersey, opened its doors on June 13, 2026, bringing together the singer’s personal musical history and a much wider exploration of America’s musical heritage. According to the centre’s official website, Monmouth University’s announcements and coverage by Artnet News, the institution has evolved considerably since its beginnings as a fan-led archival project. Its new $50 million facility spans 32,000 square feet and has been designed to serve music enthusiasts, researchers, students and the wider public.From a fan initiative to a permanent music archiveThe collection dates back to 2001, when Backstreets, a Springsteen fan magazine, organised a campaign encouraging fans to contribute newspaper articles, photographs and other material documenting different stages of the singer’s career. The initiative was driven by concerns that older media coverage and historical records were gradually disappearing.Initially known as the Bruce Springsteen Special Collection, the archive continued to grow through contributions from fans across the world. It moved to Monmouth University in 2011 and became the official repository for Springsteen’s archival material in 2017. What started as a relatively modest collection has since expanded to more than 48,000 items, according to the university’s student newspaper, The Outlook.The institution was previously called the Bruce Springsteen Archives and Center for American Music. It adopted its current name in January 2026 to reflect a broader ambition of documenting American music beyond the singer’s own career. Springsteen Center +2More than a tribute to the BossThe new building has been designed by New York-based architecture firm COOKFOX Architects, with its weathered steel exterior drawing inspiration from New Jersey’s industrial landscape. Its surroundings also reflect Springsteen’s connection to the Jersey Shore, with a boardwalk-style pathway leading visitors towards the entrance.As Artnet News reported in its June 2026 preview, the centre is structured around two complementary themes: Springsteen’s contribution to music and the wider evolution of American musical culture. The first-floor galleries explore genres and musical movements through different periods of American history. Visitors can encounter material associated with artists from different generations, including Frank Sinatra, Buddy Holly, Lady Gaga and the Beastie Boys. The displays also explore the relationship between music, technology, art and gender.A separate gallery is dedicated to temporary exhibitions, allowing the centre to introduce new themes throughout the year. Its inaugural exhibition, Chimes of Freedom: Protest, Patriotism, and the Power of Song, examines the role of music in political movements and social change across American history.Inside Springsteen’s musical worldThe second floor takes visitors closer to the musician’s personal and professional journey. The exhibits include handwritten lyrics, photographs, clothing, records and other memorabilia from different stages of his career. Among the notable displays are the jacket Springsteen wore on the cover of his 1975 album Born to Run and equipment associated with the recording of Nebraska. Another section recreates his writing room, incorporating furniture and personal belongings donated by the musician. The exhibits also explore the contributions of members of the E Street Band.The centre uses interactive installations to make the experience more immersive. Visitors can explore the creative process behind songwriting and recording, listen to different musical genres and engage with audiovisual displays. One of the highlights is a concert-inspired room that recreates the atmosphere of a live Springsteen performance through concert footage and lighting.A 241-seat theatre is another major feature of the building. It screens an approximately 25-minute documentary directed by Thom Zimny, examining the musical influences that shaped Springsteen and his place in American music.A new destination for music enthusiasts and researchersBeyond its exhibition spaces, the centre has been established as a research and educational institution. Its archival facilities are intended to support scholars, students, historians and fans interested in studying Springsteen’s work and the broader cultural significance of American music.The institution also plans to host concerts, film screenings, lectures, workshops and academic discussions, giving visitors reasons to return beyond the permanent exhibitions. Monmouth University students can access the centre free of charge with a valid university ID, although advance ticket reservations are required. The facility is open to the public, with adult admission priced at $22, according to its official visitor information.The centre’s opening marks a significant development for an archive that began with fans trying to safeguard pieces of music history. Twenty-five years later, that effort has resulted in a permanent cultural institution that documents not only Bruce Springsteen’s journey but also the artists, genres and movements that have shaped American music.You use AI every day. articles.title: Derbyshire man buys a Boeing 737 for £4,000 on Facebook and buries it beneath his garden to build an underground party bunker inspired by The Great Escape
articles.summary: A Derbyshire man has bought a Boeing 737 fuselage on Facebook for £4,000 and buried it in his back garden as part of an ambitious underground bunker
articles.body: A Derbyshire man has bought a Boeing 737 fuselage on Facebook for £4,000 and buried it in his back garden as part of an ambitious underground bunker project. Dave Billings, 45, is transforming the former Bmibaby aircraft into a hideout designed for parties, relaxation and potentially sheltering his family during a major conflict. The fuselage was lowered into a 14ft-deep excavation at his home in Hilton, where it will be connected to a network of tunnels, hidden rooms and secret entrances. The project, which has already cost at least £50,000, is inspired by The Great Escape.Boeing 737 lowered 14ft underground as part of £50,000 secret bunker projectThe aircraft has been lowered into the excavation as part of the wider underground construction project. Billings has already spent at least £50,000 on the bunker, which includes a network of tunnels, hidden rooms and concealed entrances. He believes the structure could potentially allow his family to remain off-grid for months if a major conflict broke out.Footage of the installation shows the aircraft shell being winched slowly into the ground with the help of a team. Billings also plans to install a lift shaft concealed inside a traditional red telephone box, which will provide access to the buried plane. The project has been inspired by the classic prisoner-of-war film The Great Escape.Man transforms buried Boeing into underground shelterBillings said the underground aircraft would be equipped with electricity, water, solar panels and a borehole supplying water. The plane's original toilet is also being converted into a functioning bathroom connected to the property's septic tank, while a separate ventilation system is planned for the structure.Explaining the project's intended use, Billings told the publication: "It's primarily a fun thing to have and a place for us to have parties and relax, but it could be made into a fallout shelter." He added that the aircraft would be covered with concrete and soil, leaving its top around two-and-a-half feet underground.Man reveals £13,000 extra costs to complete Boeing 737 underground bunkerBillings estimates that the construction will require a further £8,000 for concrete, £3,000 for reinforcing mesh and £2,000 for insulation before the aircraft is fully buried and secured underground. These costs are in addition to the money already spent on the wider bunker project.The engineer also plans to stock the underground space with food, drinks and beer, alongside barrels for a bar. He hopes to store enough supplies to last between three and six months. He told the publication that the bunker could remain off-grid for an extended period, depending on how much food was available.Son's love of aircraft inspires £4,000 Boeing 737 bunker purchaseBillings said his eight-year-old son Oliver, who is fascinated by aircraft, helped inspire the decision to buy the Boeing 737. His wife Beth was initially less enthusiastic about the purchase, with Billings recalling: "Beth did wonder why I was spending money on an old plane and said it was junk, but she's coming round now."Despite the bunker being designed with the possibility of a major conflict in mind, Billings said he was building it mainly for enjoyment. He said: "I'm still building this for fun at the moment." He added that he would speed up construction if circumstances changed, but said he did not believe anyone would bomb the Derbyshire Dales. The project is documented on his YouTube channel, Tornado Dave, and he hopes to finish it by February, ahead of a deadline set by his wife for their 10th wedding anniversary. articles.body: Hindu American leaders raised concerns over anti-Hindu comments on social media and incidents targeting the community across the US during a meeting with White House officials on Wednesday. They also discussed ways to improve security at Hindu temples.The White House delegation was led by faith director Jennifer Korn, visited Keshavam, a Hindu community centre and temple, and met representatives of several Hindu American organisations, according to news agency PTI.Belsis Romero, senior advisor and faith liaison at the US department of state, also joined the delegation.Representatives from Hindu Swayamsevak Sangh-USA, Sewa International, BAPS, Hindu Yuva, ISKCON, Chinmaya Mission, Art of Living, Isha Foundation, VHP of America and Shrimad Rajchandra mission attended the meeting.The Hindu American leaders spoke about the community's contributions to society. These included disaster relief work, meditation and wellness programmes, and the sewa Diwali food drive.They also raised concerns over the growing use of anti-Hindu language on social media. They highlighted incidents of hatred and discrimination against Hindus across the country.The representatives urged US officials to improve security at temples. They also called for stronger interfaith dialogue to build trust and understanding among communities.The meeting also discussed ways to increase Hindu American representation in government. Leaders stressed the need to include the community's views in federal policy discussions.“The meeting provided an opportunity for Hindu American leaders to share our community’s contributions, raise concerns, and discuss ways to strengthen engagement with the White House and federal agencies,” a participant said.Keshavam president Viswajith Mallampati had also attended diwali celebrations at the White House earlier this month.You use AI every day.
