articles.title: PUC rules changed: BS-I to BS-VI vehicles get new certificate validity periods; check yours
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The ministry of road transport and highways (MoRTH) has revised the validity period of pollution under control (PUC) certificates.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The ministry of road transport and highways (MoRTH) has revised the validity period of pollution under control (PUC) certificates. It introduced a vehicle-age-based system that will determine how frequently vehicles must undergo emission tests.Under the new rules, notified on November 13, newer BS-VI vehicles will be eligible for longer certificate validity, while older vehicles will have to undergo emission tests at shorter intervals. The revised framework also standardises PUC certificate validity for older emission categories across the country, replacing variations in testing requirements between states.The changes have been introduced through the Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, which amend Rule 115(7) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. The amendment came into force on the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.How the new rules change PUC certificate validityPreviously, the validity of a PUC certificate was determined primarily by the vehicle's Bharat Stage (BS) emission category. Consequently, a newly registered private car and an older commercial vehicle, despite belonging to the BS-VI category, were both eligible for a certificate valid for one year.The revised framework introduces a more differentiated approach for BS-VI vehicles. Certificate validity will now depend on two factors:Vehicle's ageVehicle's registration for private or commercial use.The vehicle's age will be calculated from the date of its first registration.BS-VI private vehicles: New validity periodsUnder the earlier system, all private BS-VI vehicles received PUC certificates valid for 12 months, irrespective of their age.The revised rules introduce three validity brackets:Up to six years: PUC certificate valid for three years, compared with the earlier 12 months.More than six years and up to 10 years: Validity remains unchanged at 12 months.More than 10 years: Validity reduced to six months from the earlier 12 months.This means owners of newer private BS-VI vehicles will have to undergo emission testing less frequently, while those with vehicles older than 10 years will face more frequent testing.BS-VI commercial vehicles: What changesCommercial BS-VI vehicles will also be subject to an age-based validity schedule, although the extension for newer vehicles will be shorter than that available to private vehicles.Previously, all commercial BS-VI vehicles received PUC certificates valid for one year. Under the amended rules:Up to six years: Validity increases to two years from the earlier 12 months.More than six years and up to 10 years: Validity remains at 12 months.More than 10 years: Validity is reduced to six months.The revised schedule therefore offers longer validity to newer commercial vehicles, but retains more frequent testing requirements for older ones.BS-I, II and III vehicles: 3-month testing across IndiaThe amendment also introduces a uniform testing requirement for vehicles conforming to older emission standards.Previously, BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles were generally subject to a six-month PUC certificate validity under the central rules. However, some states had prescribed shorter intervals. Delhi, for instance, already required these vehicles to undergo emission testing every three months.Under the revised framework, the validity period for all BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles will be three months, irrespective of their age or category.This makes the three-month testing requirement applicable uniformly across all states and Union territories.BS-IV vehicles: Validity reduced from one year to six monthsFor BS-IV vehicles, the earlier central provision allowed a PUC certificate validity of 12 months. However, certain states and areas within the national capital region (NCR) had already imposed a shorter six-month validity.The amended rules now prescribe six months as the standard validity period for all BS-IV vehicles across the country, irrespective of whether they are private or commercial.The change effectively brings the national requirement in line with the stricter timelines already followed in some regions.When does the validity of renewed PUC certificate beginThe amendment also clarifies how the validity period of a renewed PUC certificate will be calculated, depending on when the vehicle owner undergoes the emission test.Renewal within 10 days before expiry: If the vehicle undergoes testing within the 10 days preceding the expiry of its existing certificate, the renewed certificate will take effect from the expiry date of the previous certificate. This ensures that owners do not lose any remaining validity by renewing early.Renewal on or after expiry: If the test is conducted on or after the existing certificate's expiry date, the renewed certificate will be valid from the date of the test.Existing PUC certificates validityPUC certificates issued before the amended rules came into force will remain valid until their respective expiry dates.Vehicle owners do not need to obtain fresh certificates immediately to comply with the revised schedule. The new validity provisions will apply when they renew their existing certificates for the first time under the amended rules.For instance, a private BS-VI car that is four years old and currently holds a one-year PUC certificate will become eligible for a three-year certificate at its next renewal. The revised validity will not automatically extend the certificate it already holds.Old vs new PUC certificate validity: A comparisonEmission categoryVehicle type and ageEarlier validityNew validityBS-I, BS-II, BS-IIIAll vehicles, any age6 months (3 months in Delhi)3 monthsBS-IVAll vehicles, any age12 months (6 months in some regions)6 monthsBS-VIPrivate, up to 6 years12 months3 yearsBS-VIPrivate, over 6 to 10 years12 months12 monthsBS-VIPrivate, over 10 years12 months6 monthsBS-VICommercial, up to 6 years12 months2 yearsBS-VICommercial, over 6 to 10 years12 months12 monthsBS-VICommercial, over 10 years12 months6 monthsDocuments requiredAll vehicles must have a valid PUC certificate issued by a testing centre authorised by the respective state government.Under Rule 116 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, vehicle owners are required to produce the certificate when demanded by an authorised official. Its validity can also be verified digitally through the Parivahan PUCC Portal.Under the earlier provisions, new vehicles across emission categories were exempt from obtaining a separate PUC certificate for the first year following their initial registration. However, the available details of the latest amendment do not clarify whether this exemption has been altered or retained.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
